fanin_threshold.description: Distinct in-repo files (outside the diff) importing a changed file, at/above which lib/triage.mjs bumps the auto-computed tier one level (low→standard, standard→high; never above high). Catches a one-line change to a widely-imported module that lexical signals alone would leave at low/standard tier. Default 20; 0 disables.

always_dims.description: Dimensions (Dn ids) reviewed on every run regardless of tier — e.g. 'D16' simplification, a taste pass trimmed to opt-in below the high tier. Unknown ids are ignored. Persistent equivalent of passing them via --dimensions.

models.description: Per-dimension reviewer model selection (model = f(dimension, tier)). opus is reserved for opus_dims and only from opus_min_tier up; below that tier they use the base model. risk_map floors (via the raised tier) and an irreversible migration (D6 → opus) still apply on top.

by_tier.description: Base reviewer model per tier (default: sonnet for every tier). Keys: trivial/low/standard/high/critical → a model name.

opus_dims.description: Dimensions escalated to the strong model at opus_min_tier and above (default D3, D7, D9).

opus_min_tier.description: Lowest tier at which opus_dims run on the strong model (default 'high') — below it they use by_tier[tier].

verify.description: Bounded adversarial re-verification. Only low-confidence/uncertain aspects are re-checked; never the whole review.

max_passes_per_aspect.description: Total looks at one aspect incl. the original review (1 review + up to 2 verifier passes = 3).

reverify_below.description: Findings with confidence below this are sent to the verifier.

report_confidence.description: Findings at/above this survive to the report.

escalate_uncertain.description: Still-uncertain after the cap → surface to the human, do not drop.

model_first.description: Model for the first (cheap) verifier pass. Default 'sonnet'.

model_escalate.description: Model the verifier escalates to on an uncertain or hot-refuted verdict, and runs directly for the severities in escalate_direct_severity. Its verdict is authoritative — the cheap one is discarded. Default 'opus'.

escalate_direct_severity.description: Severities that skip the cheap pass and go straight to model_escalate. Default ['critical'].

max_verifier_agents.description: Per-run cap on batched verifier groups (default per-tier: trivial 0, low 3, standard 5, high/critical 8). An explicit flat value here wins over the per-tier default; by_tier.<tier>.max_verifier_agents wins over both.

by_tier.description: Per-tier overrides of the verify keys above. A tier entry (trivial/low/standard/high/critical) overrides the flat keys for that resolved tier; the flat keys stay the base. reverify_below is clamped up to report_confidence per tier so a per-tier relaxation can lower both together (fewer verifier spawns) but never opens a [reverify_below, report_confidence) dead band. Defaults keep 80/80 on every tier, so worst-case rigor is unchanged unless a project opts in here.

escalation.description: Spawn-on-doubt: when a reviewer flags uncertain:true, fan a tiny panel (capped) at just that aspect.

max_review_aspects.description: Ceiling on total review aspects (≈ reviewer agents) for a sharded diff; shard count is reduced to fit so a many-dimension change never spawns a runaway fan-out. Default 40.

max_review_files.description: Hard ceiling on the number of changed files actually reviewed. args.json — which the orchestrator model must emit verbatim into the Workflow call — grows one entry per reviewed file (shards/sliceIndex/diffIndex), so past a point the generation drops mid-response. When a diff exceeds this, the highest-risk files (on a risk path first, then largest changes) are kept and the rest dropped, with a WARN in the report that some files were not reviewed. Default 200.

mega_pr.description: Two-stage funnel (#10) for a change far beyond large_diff.max_review_files. Below `threshold`, this is a no-op — selectReviewFiles's blunt cap behaves exactly as before. Above it, every risk-path file and every file not part of a qualifying 'mechanical cluster' (files sharing a top-level directory + extension, at least cluster_min of them, with per-file LOC churn all within churn_tolerance of the cluster's median) is reviewed in full; each mechanical cluster is instead deterministically sampled (always including its highest-churn file). Heuristic, not a diff-similarity proof — a conservative first cut for mega-PRs (300+ files) with no prior precedent in this codebase.

threshold.description: File count above which the funnel engages instead of selectReviewFiles's blind cap. Default 250 — deliberately higher than max_review_files' default (200) so this never fires for a change today's existing cap would already have fully covered.

cluster_min.description: Minimum files in a (top-dir, extension) group for it to be considered for sampling at all; smaller groups stay fully hot. Default 8.

churn_tolerance.description: Fractional tolerance (default 0.3 = ±30%) around a group's median per-file LOC churn; any file outside the band disqualifies the whole group from being treated as mechanical.

sample_rate.description: Fraction of a qualifying mechanical cluster to sample (default 0.15), subject to cluster_min_sample as a floor.

cluster_min_sample.description: Minimum files sampled from a qualifying mechanical cluster regardless of sample_rate. Default 3.

diff_scope.description: Diff-scope demotion: a finding anchored more than `slack` lines outside the changed hunks (on a changed file) is demoted to an advisory 'Out-of-scope observations' section — excluded from the verdict, gate, and --comment. Findings on unchanged files are always demoted; line-less findings on changed files are never demoted.

slack.description: Lines of tolerance above/below a hunk before a finding is treated as out-of-diff (default 3).

scan.description: Run real tools when available (advisory; findings feed D15).

tests.description: Test-execution signal (S6.4). With `/review --run-tests` the plugin runs `command` after checkout and feeds pass/fail + failing test NAMES (never logs) to the test-adequacy-reviewer (D5) and the report header. The command is NEVER guessed — it runs only when set here. It EXECUTES repo code; do not use --run-tests on an untrusted PR. Off by default (no --run-tests flag).

command.description: The project's own test command, e.g. 'npm test' or 'pytest -q'.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the test command after this many ms (default 600000).

completeness.description: High-tier completeness SCREEN (S6.1): a cheap sonnet false-negative screen that flags dimension/criterion COVERAGE gaps (it sees no diff, so not taint). Runs on the high tier only, and only when the full exhaustive critic is not already running.

screen_on_high.description: Run the high-tier completeness screen (default true). Set false to skip the extra sonnet pass.

fanout.description: Lever D — fan-out trim (agent-count cost lever). OFF by default. When trim:true, the content-gated specialist reviewers (the net-new dimensions beyond the tier's base set) are deferred/capped to cut how many reviewer subagents fan out on sub-high tiers. Base-tier dimensions and always_dims are never trimmed; a dropped dimension is stated in the report's 'Did not run' section. Complements the sonnet-first verify and per-file diff slicing cost levers. The critical tier is never trimmed regardless of these settings.

trim.description: Master switch. false (default) = no trimming, identical to prior behavior.

defer_dims.description: Advisory specialist dimensions deferred to defer_below+ (default ["D9","D17"] — perf & a11y). Their content signal on a sub-high change is usually covered by the correctness screen; they return at the floor tier and above.

defer_below.description: Tier floor for defer_dims (default "high"): below this tier the deferred dimensions are dropped even if their signal fires.

max_added.description: Cap on the number of content-gated specialists added beyond the tier's base set (default: uncapped). When exceeded, the lowest-priority dimensions are dropped (priority: security/data > correctness > contract/deps/advisory).

keep_order.description: Override the drop-priority ranking for max_added (dims listed earlier are kept first).

checkout.description: Detach HEAD onto the remote's latest pushed head for the review (restored afterwards), so the reviewers see the most recent pushed code rather than the local checkout. The reviewed diff is the GitHub-exact fork-point (three-dot) range by default. Disable to review the working tree in place.

fork_point.description: Review the GitHub-exact three-dot range merge-base(base,head)..head (default true). Set false to review the two-dot base..head instead (includes base's newer commits when the branch is behind).

learning.description: Per-project memory: recurring findings, accepted false-positives, and unresolved questions persist across runs.

feedback.description: PR-reaction feedback loop (WS2): after --comment posts an inline finding comment, comments.mjs seeds both 👍/👎 reactions so a one-click vote is possible; a later review of the same PR harvests non-seed reactions + reply text via feedback.mjs and folds them into the learnings store (learning.store) — 👎 becomes an accepted false-positive (also injected pre-generation into future reviewer packets as a known-false-positive block); 👍 alone is a no-op, recording no signal and never skipping verification. Gated by learning.enabled (no store, no harvest).

store.description: Path to the posted-comment-id state file (default '.adversarial-code-review/posted-comments.json').

rereview.description: Re-review convergence (WS3): on a later review of the same PR, resolved findings get their GitHub thread replied-to-and-resolved, persisting findings are never re-posted, and this block tunes how aggressively nits taper off across rounds.

nit_rounds.description: Number of re-review rounds (starting at 1, the first review) minor/suggestion findings still post as PR comments. From round nit_rounds+1 on they are report-only. Default 1 (Anthropic's REVIEW.md guidance: important-only after round 1).

report.description: Report-rendering knobs that are not part of the gate/verify policy.

max_posted_nits.description: Cap on how many minor/suggestion findings comments.mjs posts as PR comments in one run (top-N by confidence; default 5). The report file always lists every finding regardless — this only trims PR-comment noise.

ask_on_unresolved.description: Surface unresolved/assumption questions to the user instead of silently assuming.

trackers.description: Issue-tracker key patterns. Tickets are fetched via MCP by the orchestrator — no API tokens are stored or used.

exhaustive.description: Tier C ultrareview-parity passes (completeness critic, D3 taint verifier, and a double run of the correctness + vuln reviewers unioned by finding). Auto-on at the critical tier or with --exhaustive; they cost extra tokens.

on_critical.description: Run the exhaustive passes automatically when the tier is critical (default true).

usage.description: Token-usage + USD-cost panel shown top-left of review.html. Summed from this run's session transcripts within the review window.

enabled.description: Show the usage panel (default true). Set false to omit it.

pricing.description: Override the per-model-family price table (USD per million tokens). Each family overlays the defaults field-by-field; omit a field to keep the default.

verifyTier.description: Per-tier subset of the verify keys. Only the keys set here override the flat verify policy for that tier.
